course_title: IC Design Process: Beginner's VLSI Overview

slides.title: Course Goal: From Code to Chip
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome to this beginner's overview of VLSI technology! Our core goal is to bridge the gap, connecting what you write in Hardware Description Languages to the actual silicon circuit. This course offers a theoretical, high-level understanding of the entire IC design and manufacturing process, without focusing on specific coding.

slides.title: ICs: Definition & Evolution
points: IC: Many circuits on tiny silicon.
SoC: Full electronic system on one chip.
Replaced vacuum tubes, then discrete transistors.
slides.speaker_notes: An Integrated Circuit, or IC, places numerous electronic circuits onto a tiny silicon plate. A System-on-Chip, or SoC, integrates a complete electronic system, housing billions of transistors. This evolved from bulky vacuum tubes, then discrete transistors, to today's compact, integrated designs on a single silicon piece.

slides.title: VLSI: Scale & Impact
points: Integration scaled from few to billions.
VLSI: universal term for high-density ICs.
slides.speaker_notes: IC integration evolved from just tens of components in Small-Scale Integration, or SSI, to millions and eventually billions of transistors. While stages like MSI and LSI marked this growth, today, all advanced, high-density IC manufacturing is universally termed Very Large Scale Integration, or VLSI.

slides.title: Digital Circuits: Core Concepts
points: Two types: Sequential (with memory) and Combinational.
slides.speaker_notes: Digital circuits convert data to binary, using voltage states for 0s and 1s. Transistors are their fundamental building blocks, acting as simple on/off switches. We distinguish between combinational circuits, where output depends solely on current inputs, and sequential circuits, which include memory and depend on past inputs.

slides.title: Building Blocks of Digital ICs
points: Digital circuits break down to logic gates & flip-flops.
Flip-flops are made of logic gates.
All logic gates are made of transistors.
slides.speaker_notes: Digital circuits are constructed from two primary components: logic gates and flip-flops. Flip-flops, which store a single bit of data, are themselves built using various logic gates. Ultimately, every single logic gate, like NAND or NOR, is fundamentally realized using combinations of transistors. This forms a hierarchical structure.

slides.title: HDLs: Abstracting Complexity
points: HDLs model circuits, hiding transistor details.
slides.speaker_notes: In summary, all digital circuits are ultimately built from a vast number of transistors, forming gates and flip-flops. Managing this complexity demands abstraction. Hardware Description Languages, or HDLs, allow us to model these intricate circuits at a higher level, effectively hiding the overwhelming transistor-level details.
